Task for gpt-6.1-sol xhigh. User now explicitly wants FACTORY/DEFAULT original ESP-IDF rates on same S31/Korvo, multiple runs then mean/range into expected targets in markdown. Existing korvo-reference is NOT this: custom E70 FS geometry/yield + patched iperf and hybrid network config. Root owns board/USB/serial/Windows/network/credentials/recovery. You perform OFFLINE code/config/build preparation only. Preserve SDK, old snapshots, dirty trees, old measured data and current openvela source. No hardware or network access; no downloads/upgrades. Read root README and relevant documents.

Create isolated diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference only (do not modify old project); reuse locked SDK, local upstream littlefs wrapper/core archives and original official iperf component. Need exact upstream source identity, no modifications to SDK/Wi-Fi/lwIP/flash driver/LittleFS wrapper/core or official iperf library. Existing source + archives and hashes at diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-reference/evidence, source originals in local cache/predecessor projects; inspect rather than invent. Current vendor library hashes frozen. Restore wrapper original content from pinned local archive, never reverse-patch uncertain versions. Preserve library's own stock build CMake if possible; any local component registration glue separate and documented.

Defaults mean SDK Kconfig DEFAULTS (not official high-performance iperf sdkconfig, which expands buffers and disables watchdog/PLL tracking). Minimal overrides only necessary S31 target, verified board UART pins58/59, flash physical16MiB/known compatible mode at native default speed, safe partition layout factory0x10000 and synthetic FS0x500000 size7MiB, app stack if genuinely needed, no persistent credentials/NVS/calibration writes outside authorized layout, local dependency resolution. Normal default CPU/tick/compiler/Wi-Fi buffers/socket/BA/affinity remain defaults. Runtime Wi-Fi use default protocol/bandwidth/power saving, only STA mode, RAM storage and authorized AP/BSSID pin. Do not force BGN/BW20/PS_NONE to match openvela; if default negotiation differs report actual. Keep default watchdog and PHY tracking protections; do not inject yield into filesystem callbacks or measured loops, disable watchdog, or silently change task priority to improve results.

FS: upstream LittleFS component defaults (including mtime), no E70 geometry overrides, no VFS coalescing cache. Keep same 5.1.7 800000B/1000x20B read/10x20B write, 5.1.11 4096Bx64 seq/random all-A with seed1 and5.1.12 dd-equivalent262144B, same setup/remount validation and loop/fflush-fsync-close timing. Exclude validation delays from speed figures; record any setup app yield as setup only. Preserve full verification and safe7MiB geometry check; each FS ALL fresh formats this temporary volume, never autoformat remount. Existing fs_bench code can be copied with only stale static assertion/config mapping removed and no timed-path instrumentation. If pristine default original workload risks watchdog, document and leave original behavior, don't 'fix' reference by modifying it; Root will classify real failure if occurs.

NET: official untouched iperf implementation with minimum application wrapper using public APIs only; no per-packet counters/callback patches/FIN changes. Original official example reports may have EOF/FIN limitations; retain/report these, don't require custom diagnostic marker a stock library cannot produce. Use receiver native goodput and actual offered rate if available. Need four30s directions to original pinned host executable, UDP1470 and40M command, TCP original comparable buffer workload. Default socket/Wi-Fi config must remain stock; if user buffer sizes provided via public test CLI this is workload, document it. Don't put passwords in firmware/config/logs, reuse private runtime binary credential input/WIFI_STORAGE_RAM from old wrapper. Public wrapper must clear its RAM copies, support WIFI_OFF, status and bounded STOP/timeout/cleanup without touching vendor component implementation. AP link actual data printed safely.

Keep console protocol minimally compatible with existing FS runner and UART transaction; distinct DEFAULTREF identity. Produce concrete protocol notes to permit Root adapter reuse. We need board readiness in smallest scope, not another elaborate framework. Build fully offline with actual paired SDK outputs, fixed flash offsets and hash receipt, original source manifests, resolved DEFAULT-vs-required-override audit. Run only meaningful build/host checks for changed wrapper boundaries/credential redaction/config/partition safety. Do not emulate throughput or claim board pass. Deliver frozen build + exact necessary override list + any blockers. Root will review then execute three valid repeats and restore.

I’ll inspect the local guidance, pinned sources and existing harness, then prepare and freeze `korvo-default-reference` offline. I’ll keep all changes in that new directory and leave hardware, network and existing projects untouched.

The existing reference confirms the differences you flagged: E70 LittleFS settings, callback yields, patched iperf, and CPU/network tuning. I’ll restore LittleFS from its pinned archive and check the predecessor’s official iperf files against the recorded upstream hashes before using them.

The pinned S31 Kconfig defaults select DIO/80 MHz, CPU 320 MHz, a 100 Hz tick, debug optimization and 5760-byte TCP buffers. I’ve left those settings alone. I’m also resolving a separate empty-default configuration for an exact override audit. The FS setup’s 4000-byte local record array already exceeds the default 3584-byte main stack, so I’ve set the main stack to 8192 bytes.

The first target build compiled and linked successfully with the stock LittleFS and iperf CMake files. The resolved config keeps LittleFS mtime enabled and uses its default 128-byte read/program sizes, 512-byte cache and 128-byte lookahead.

Stock iperf provides no public listener-ready callback or FIN diagnostics. I’ll retain its native reports and document the runner changes needed to use them. The wrapper’s completion marker will report lifecycle completion only.

The build receipt now contains the paired image hashes and fixed offsets. The audit found exactly 22 resolved configuration differences, all from the required board, layout, persistence and stack settings. The freeze checks also verify the upstream sources, stock library hashes, built partition table and unchanged FS loops.

The protocol notes and three-run mean/range table are written. The table remains pending Root’s measurements; no rates or board passes have been inferred.

Prepared and froze [korvo-default-reference](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference/README.md) entirely offline.

- Full build and host boundary checks passed; upstream sources, vendor hashes and FS timed paths verified unchanged.
- [Exact override audit](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference/config-audit.md) documents the required board/layout/persistence/stack changes.
- [Build receipt](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference/evidence/build-receipt.json) binds paired images, offsets and hashes.
- [Protocol notes](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference/protocol.md) explain adapter reuse and stock iperf limitations.

No offline build blockers. No hardware/network access or board-pass claim. The [mean/range table](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-default-reference/expected-targets.md) awaits Root’s three valid repeats.
